verses.text: Then Solomon began to build the LORD's temple in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to his father David. It was on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, the place David had prepared.
He began building on the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his rule.
These are the measurements Solomon used for the foundation of God's temple, using the old standard measure. It was about twenty-seven metres long and nine metres wide.
The porch at the front of the temple was nine metres wide, the same as the width of the temple, and fifty-four metres high. He covered the inside with pure gold.
He lined the main room with pine boards and covered them with fine gold. He decorated it with palm trees and chain designs.
He decorated the temple with precious stones to make it beautiful. The gold he used came from Parvaim.
He covered the ceiling beams, the doorframes, the walls, and the doors of the temple with gold, and he carved cherubim on the walls.
He built the Most Holy Place. It was nine metres long, the same as the width of the temple, and nine metres wide. He covered it with about twenty tonnes of fine gold.
The gold nails weighed about six hundred grams. He also covered the upper rooms with gold.
In the Most Holy Place he made two carved cherubim and covered them with gold.

The total length of the cherubim's wings was nine metres. One wing of the first cherub was over two metres long and touched the wall of the temple. Its other wing, also over two metres long, touched a wing of the second cherub.
One wing of the second cherub was over two metres long and touched the other wall of the temple. Its other wing, also over two metres long, touched the wing of the first cherub.
The wings of these cherubim stretched out nine metres in all. The cherubim stood on their feet, facing the main room.
He made the curtain of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine linen, with cherubim woven into it.
In front of the temple he made two pillars, about sixteen metres tall. Each had a top piece over two metres high.
He made chains like a necklace and put them on top of the pillars. He made a hundred pomegranates and attached them to the chains.
He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the south side and one on the north. He named the one on the south Jakin and the one on the north Boaz.
